tells: The idea fits the subject: early-computing hardware and the people who built it are shown through scan-line glitch, a silicon die and a glowing red disc that resolves into the 'HALT AND CATCH FIRE' title card

A deliberate, almost monochrome palette runs from hot pink to oxblood, with one cream accent in the chip-quad frame
The choreography builds: abstract glitch, then a silhouetted portrait, then a macro of the chip, then the title. The sense of scale changes every beat
The credits are set in a restrained classic serif, which contrasts with a heavy wide-caps title. That pairing is a choice, not a default
gaps: The credit typography is placed passively in the lower third and never interacts with the image the way A's type does

The frames are less varied in composition, with several relying on a centred object on red. Bolder framing or asymmetry would turn more frames into posters
